claims.text: Phase stability in Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni high-entropy alloys is governed by the grain-boundary character distribution.
Grain-boundary character distribution affects high-temperature strength in Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni alloys.
Grain-boundary character distribution affects environmental resistance in Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni alloys.
Grain-boundary character distribution affects radiation tolerance in Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni alloys.
Grain-boundary character distribution affects cryogenic toughness in Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni alloys.
Thermomechanical processing followed by heat treatment will alter the grain-boundary character distribution.
Changing the grain-boundary character distribution will change phase stability.
An optimized grain-boundary character distribution will improve high-temperature strength relative to an alloy without grain-boundary engineering.
An optimized grain-boundary character distribution will improve environmental resistance relative to an alloy without grain-boundary engineering.
An optimized grain-boundary character distribution will improve radiation tolerance relative to an alloy without grain-boundary engineering.
An optimized grain-boundary character distribution will improve cryogenic toughness relative to an alloy without grain-boundary engineering.
